$schema_note: One row per product a searcher compares against Grok Bot. Every value carries the URL it was read from and the date it was read. `scripts/refresh.py` re-reads the machine-checkable fields (licence, archived, last push) from the GitHub API and prints what moved; it never writes a claim the source does not publish.

columns.isolation_unit: What one agent/session gets on its own: a machine, a container, a process, or nothing (one shared machine).

columns.review_gate: What stands between an agent's change and production: a diff a person merges, an approval card, or nothing.

sources.quote: Every Grok Bot shares one persistent cloud computer. Your Bots share that machine (files, browser, logins), so they can hand work off and keep context. Isolation is per user, not per Grok Bot.
Hosting Grok Bot runs only on Cursor-hosted cloud computers. On-premises deployment, deployment inside your own perimeter, and bring-your-own-image deployment are not supported today.
An approval controls the proposed action. It does not reverse work already completed.
